name: Lloyds Metals and Energy Ltd
thesis: Financially clean iron-ore-to-steel compounder at peak-cycle earnings: standalone FY26 sales ₹13,681cr, PAT ₹3,194cr (+120%), CFO ₹4,816cr (1.51× PAT), 5.9-day receivables, zero earnings-quality trips. The pellet ramp (3.03 MnT, 100% utilisation in 4 months) and slurry pipeline structurally lifted mix — value-added products went from 20%→32% of revenue, 11%→30% of EBIT. But the market prices all of it at 33× FY26 EPS / 25× TTM EPS, 165% above the derating-aware DCF anchor. Commodity cyclical, heavy capex, rising consolidated leverage — quality company, wrong price.
risks: 165% above DCF fair value; 25× TTM EPS on record earnings — peak-cycle multiple
Consolidated leverage: net debt ~₹19,000cr (Thriveni acquisition debt + Chemaf); standalone borrowings ₹5,504cr
Capex dam: ₹8,131cr spent FY26, ~₹11,000cr more over 2 years — execution risk
Promoter NDUs Aug–Sep 2026 (Thriveni 2.80%, Shreekrishna Gupta 16% of his holding, LLP) for term-loan financing — encumbrance creep outside the SHP pledge count
Iron-ore price cyclicality; Gadchiroli concentration; DRC/Chemaf Africa exposure
NTPC receivable dispute unresolved (mgmt: 2–3 months, Aug-2026 concall)

promises.promise: FY26: record scale — iron ore 21.96 MnT, pellet ramp
FY27 guidance: iron ore 26 MnT, pellets 7.75–8 MnT, DRI 825 KT, WRM 0.15–0.2 MnT, copper 10–12kt
promises.delivery: 🔄 In progress (Q1FY27: record quarter, volumes nearly doubled YoY)

promises.promise: 2nd pellet plant commissioned May-2026 on schedule/within budget
Copper: commercial cathode production from Mar-2026 (12,000 TPA DRC)
